content: Individuals with preexisting diabetes who are planning to become pregnant should ideally receive comprehensive preconception care from a multidisciplinary team. This team should include specialists in endocrinology, maternal-fetal medicine, nutrition, and diabetes education. Glycated hemoglobin (A1C) levels and glycemic targets should be established well in advance of conception to optimize outcomes. Preconception care should encompass a thorough evaluation and management of glycemic targets, nutritional needs, physical activity, and lifestyle factors. Additionally, it should include screening for and addressing any complications related to diabetes, such as nephropathy, neuropathy, or retinopathy. Effective contraception should be utilized until the individual is fully prepared to conceive, ensuring optimal health conditions for both the mother and the fetus. For individuals with type 1 or type 2 diabetes who are planning a pregnancy, a comprehensive eye examination should be performed, ideally before conception or during the first trimester of pregnancy. Follow-up eye exams should be conducted as clinically indicated, based on the severity of diabetic retinopathy, to monitor and manage any progression of the condition during pregnancy.
